package_info.why_malicious: The package was updated after a long dormant period to include code that establishes persistence and exfiltrates potential Ethereum private keys from the clipboard to a remote server. The updates introduced installation hooks and scripts that monitor the clipboard for 64-character strings (matching Ethereum private key format) and send them to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the package executes a benign-looking JavaScript function and then runs a PowerShell script, setting up the persistence mechanism.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Installation hooks are used to execute code unrelated to the package's stated functionality, especially invoking PowerShell scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not execute arbitrary scripts or set up persistence during install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use install hooks for setup or compilation, but not for persistence or running PowerShell.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the script writes a batch file to the Windows Startup folder that will execute a PowerShell script on user login, establishing persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Writing to the Startup folder is a classic persistence technique for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A development tool should not create autorun scripts in the user's Startup folder.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate software may set up auto-start for background services, but not in this context.
key_indicators: Creates batch file to launch PowerShell

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At user login, the script runs in an infinite loop, monitoring the clipboard for 64-character strings (potential Ethereum private keys) and exfiltrates them via HTTP POST to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Continuous clipboard monitoring and exfiltration of data to an external server is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate reason for a gas reporting tool to monitor clipboard or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Clipboard managers may monitor clipboard, but never exfiltrate to remote servers.

attack_chain.action: During installation, package.json hooks execute PowerShell script to set up persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence mechanism established via Startup folder.

attack_chain.action: On user login, system.bat launches NewFile.ps1, which begins clipboard monitoring.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continuous clipboard surveillance for sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: If clipboard contains a 64-character string, it is exfiltrated to attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives potential Ethereum private keys.

behavioral_signatures: npm package install triggers PowerShell script execution
Creation of batch or PowerShell scripts in Windows Startup folder
Outbound HTTP POST requests to suspicious endpoints from PowerShell
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for unexpected install hooks invoking PowerShell. Detect creation of autorun scripts in the Windows Startup folder. Flag processes that continuously access the clipboard and send data to external endpoints, especially if targeting 64-character strings. Block or alert on outbound connections to known malicious endpoints such as test-lake-delta-49.vercel.app/keys.
